use std::sync::{Arc, Barrier};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
fn main() {
    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<usize>(), 8);
    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<AtomicUsize>(), 8);
    assert_eq!(std::mem::align_of::<AtomicUsize>(), 8);
    for _ in 0..16 {
        // SAFETY: Flux allocates, initializes, and later destroys its own cell;
        // the host sees only an opaque pointer and never guesses its layout.
        let p = unsafe { make_cell() } as usize;
        assert_ne!(p, 0);
        assert_eq!(unsafe { probe_cell(p as *mut u8) }, 0);
        let control = Arc::new([AtomicUsize::new(0), AtomicUsize::new(0)]);
        let barrier = Arc::new(Barrier::new(9));
        let threads: Vec<_> = (1..=8).map(|seed| {
            let control = control.clone();
            let barrier = barrier.clone();
            std::thread::spawn(move || {
                barrier.wait();
                // SAFETY: all scalar signatures were audited against Keel IR.
                // Arc pins the control words, touched only atomically by both
                // compilers. The cell remains live until all workers join.
                unsafe { worker_cell(p as *mut u8, control.as_ptr() as *mut usize, seed) }
            })
        }).collect();
        barrier.wait();
        while control[0].load(Ordering::Relaxed) == 0 { std::thread::yield_now(); }
        assert_eq!(unsafe { probe_cell(p as *mut u8) }, 0);
        control[1].store(1, Ordering::Release);
        let values: Vec<_> = threads.into_iter().map(|t| t.join().unwrap()).collect();
        assert!((1..=8).contains(&values[0]));
        assert!(values.iter().all(|v| *v == values[0]));
        assert_eq!(control[0].load(Ordering::Relaxed), 1);
        assert_eq!(unsafe { probe_cell(p as *mut u8) }, 1);
        assert_eq!(unsafe { free_cell(p as *mut u8) }, 0);
    }
    println!("Flux one winner / nonblocking get / payload publication ok");
}
